novelty.justification: The novelty route is primarily a new measurement and error decomposition: the claim proposes a per-problem “specification gap” and asks whether an apparent failure is actually “correct reasoning over a silently mis-chosen interpretation,” identified when an answer matches a valid alternative reading. Searches for “LLM ambiguous math word problems alternative interpretations,” “semantic underspecification reasoning errors precisification,” and “specification gap LLM reasoning” found closely related ambiguity work including AmbigQA, Stengel-Eskin et al.’s “We’re Afraid Language Models Aren’t Modeling Ambiguity,” and SCICONVBENCH, which already studies silent assumptions and disambiguation failures, but not the systematic alternative-reading answer attribution across several reasoning families proposed here. The step is therefore a substantive natural extension and multi-part operationalization—not a new paradigm or wholly new phenomenon—because it combines known ambiguity/disambiguation ideas with a distinct specification-gap predictor and interpretation-versus-reasoning error partition.
